title: Have your bot phone a company to cancel a subscription
summary: Some cancellations are easier by phone than through endless web forms. With a phone-calling add-on, your bot can make the call for you and report back.
what_the_bot_does: Gets a phone number of its own through a calling add-on you connect.
Looks up the company's cancellation line and the account details it will need.
Calls, says up front that it's an AI assistant calling for you, and asks to cancel.
Turns down retention offers unless you said you'd accept one.
Tells you what was said and saves any confirmation number.
what_you_end_up_with: The subscription cancelled (or a clear answer why not) and a confirmation number, without you sitting on hold.

tools.note: Needs a phone-calling add-on connected; the shared example used one

prompt: Call [company] at their customer service line and cancel my [subscription name]. My account details: [name on account, email, last 4 of card if needed]. Start the call by saying you're an AI assistant calling on my behalf. Turn down any discount or pause offer unless it's [what you'd accept]. Don't agree to anything that costs money. Afterwards, tell me what they said and give me the confirmation number.
watch_out: Some companies won't act for anyone but the account holder. One user says an airline refused to rebook his flight for exactly that reason.
Have the bot announce it's an AI. One user says a restaurant owner almost hung up on his bot, thinking it was spam, until it identified itself.
A phone call is harder to undo than an email, so be specific about what the bot may agree to.
Check your next statement to make sure the charges actually stopped.
